sources.massKg: TUNING KNOB — 2,857 kg (6,300 lb), the T-6A Texan II published max gross weight (single PT6A-68 turboprop military/civil trainer). Source verification pending (issue #8 — owner starting-list item).
sources.wingAreaM2: 16.69 m^2 (179.6 sq ft published T-6A reference wing area); wing loading ~171 kg/m^2 at 2,857 kg. Source verification pending.
sources.wingSpanM: 10.19 m (33 ft 5 in published T-6A span). Source verification pending; consistent with aspectRatio: b^2/S = 10.19^2/16.69 = 6.22.
sources.aspectRatio: 6.22 — a low-AR trainer wing (aerobatic-capable, not the King Air's efficient-cruise high-AR wing); b^2/S = 10.19^2/16.69 = 6.22.
sources.cl0: TUNING KNOB (stall band) — 0.20 zero-AoA lift for a moderately cambered trainer wing.
sources.clAlphaPerRad: TUNING KNOB (stall band) — 5.2/rad. Pinned by the offline force-balance check against the T-6A's published ~80 kt clean stall.
sources.stallAlphaRad: TUNING KNOB (stall band) — 15.5 deg (0.27 rad) clean critical AoA; CLmax_clean = 0.20 + 5.2*0.27 = 1.60. Gives a clean stall of ~80 kt at 2,857 kg (Vstall = sqrt(2*W/(rho*S*CLmax))), matching the published T-6A clean stall band (~78-88 kt depending on config). Pinned alongside clAlphaPerRad.
sources.postStallDecayRad: TUNING KNOB — 0.18 rad fade width past the break, matching the biz/tprop pattern.
sources.cd0: TUNING KNOB (cruise TAS + SL climb + ceiling) — 0.026, a trainer-class clean parasite-drag coefficient: draggier than the King Air's 0.028-per-larger-wing figure is not comparable directly, but on this smaller wing it holds a ~291 kt TAS cruise at FL200/90% power and a ~3,100 fpm sea-level climb (offline force-balance check, matching the T-6A's published ~3,100+ fpm initial climb) while still producing a real, barely-climbing ceiling (~170 fpm) at the certified 31,000 ft service ceiling. Source verification pending.
sources.gearDragCd0: TUNING KNOB — 0.02 retractable tricycle-gear increment, matching the tprop/biz convention.
sources.speedbrakeCd0: 0.0 — the T-6A has no airbrake/spoiler, so this increment is honestly zero (num(), not positive(), so 0 is legal — mirrors tprop's King Air).
sources.oswaldE: TUNING KNOB — 0.75, a modest span efficiency for a low-AR trainer wing (below the King Air's 0.80 high-AR figure).
sources.cyBeta: TUNING KNOB — -0.60/rad single-engine trainer side-force slope.
sources.rollRateMaxRadS: TUNING KNOB — ~149 deg/s, the T-6A's aerobatic-capable roll rate (decisions B-007 pattern): well above the King Air's 40 deg/s, below the F-5E's fighter 200 deg/s — an unaugmented but nimble trainer.
sources.damping/stiffness: TUNING KNOBS — pitch omega_n = sqrt(3.5) = 1.87 rad/s, zeta = 3.0/(2*1.87) = 0.80 (well damped, crisp trainer feel).
sources.refDynamicPressurePa: TUNING KNOB — 5000 Pa, above the King Air's 3500 Pa (a faster trainer reaches full control authority at a higher speed) and below the bizjet's 6500 Pa.
sources.trimAlphaCenterRad: TUNING KNOB — 1.4 deg, near cruise AoA.
sources.trimAlphaRangeRad: TUNING KNOB — +-16.0 deg trim authority. Wide enough that full aft stick/trim can pull past the 15.5 deg clean stall AoA — an honest aerobatic-trainer envelope, and pinned by the g-clamp envelope test (a fast-entry full pull must actually reach the published +7.0g limit before the wing runs out of CLmax; a narrower range left the pull ~9% short of 7g at a 250 kt entry).
sources.propulsion: TUNING KNOBS — single flat-rated turboprop via the shared power-limited-PROP formula T=eta*P/max(V,propPeakSpeedMs) (same formula as tprop/C172, not the flat-rated-turbofan constant-thrust form): propPeakSpeedMs 90 m/s sits below cruise TAS (~150 m/s) so cruise thrust falls with speed like a real prop. maxPowerW 820,000 W = 1,100 shp flat-rated PT6A-68 (SOURCED: 1,100 shp * 745.7 W/shp = 820,270 W, the T-6A's published engine rating). eta*P/peak = 0.85*820000/90 = 7.75 kN full-throttle static-band thrust; T/W ~0.28 at 2,857 kg. afterburnerFactor 1.0 (none).
sources.propPeakSpeedMs: TUNING KNOB (climb + cruise) — 90 m/s (175 kt): below cruise TAS so cruise thrust falls with speed, above best-climb TAS so the efficiency ramp caps SL climb to the plausible ~3,100 fpm the T-6A publishes.
sources.propEfficiency: 0.85 — the eta in T = eta*P/max(V,peak), matching the other turboprop/piston classes.
sources.lapseModel: "turboprop" — same flat-rated-shaft-power lapse as tprop (decisions.md TP-001); a single PT6A is the same engine family as the King Air's PT6A-60A, just smaller.
sources.turbopropCornerM: TUNING KNOB (ceiling) — 5,500 m (~FL180), below tprop's 6,858 m corner: the T-6A's lower 31,000 ft certified ceiling (vs the King Air's 35,000 ft) needs its shaft power to start lapsing sooner. Offline force-balance check: best climb at 31,000 ft measures ~170 fpm — a real, barely-climbing ceiling. Not a published PT6A-68 figure; source verification pending.
sources.turbopropLapseExp: TUNING KNOB (ceiling) — 2.2, close to tprop's 2.5 stratospheric falloff exponent. Not a published figure.
sources.limits.vneIasMs: TUNING KNOB — ~320 KIAS = 164.6 m/s, a plausible Vne for the T-6A's published ~316 KTAS max speed band. Source verification pending.
sources.limits.vnoIasMs: TUNING KNOB — ~280 KIAS = 144.0 m/s display caution reference below Vne.
sources.limits.vfeIasMs: TUNING KNOB — ~150 KIAS = 77.2 m/s flap placard; display only.
sources.mmo: TUNING KNOB — 0.60, well subsonic (the T-6A never approaches transonic speeds; spec §1/§7 has no wave-drag physics regardless).
sources.vleIasMs: TUNING KNOB — ~150 KIAS = 77.2 m/s Vle/Vlo placard; display only. Set equal to vfeIasMs (a plausible single combined gear/flap-speed placard for a light trainer); source verification pending.
sources.gLimits: +7.0 / -3.5 — the T-6A's published aerobatic/utility-category load-factor limits (a genuinely aerobatic-capable trainer, between the biz's +3.0 transport limit and the F-5E's +7.33 fighter limit).
sources.serviceCeilingM: 9,448.8 m (31,000 ft) — the T-6A's published certified service ceiling. Made honest in-model by the turboprop lapse (turbopropCornerM 5500 + turbopropLapseExp 2.2): full-throttle best climb there measures ~170 fpm, a real barely-climbing ceiling.
sources.flaps: 0/APPR/FULL — simplified trainer schedule mirroring tprop; dCL0/dStallAlpha/dCD0 are TUNING KNOBS giving monotonically falling stall speeds and rising drag.
sources.display: ASI 40-350 kt spans the trainer band (faster top end than the King Air, slower than the jets); attitudeStyle ball — the T-6A has a modern all-glass EFIS cockpit (Rockwell Collins Pro Line 21), unlike the King Air's steam-gauge six-pack, so it shares the jets' full attitude-disc rendering.
sources.gear: retractable — the T-6A has retractable tricycle gear.
